translation_notes: region is a statement run at module level: `state`, `graph` and `ns_rdf` come from context_shim.py (subset of the pyRdfa execution context, `state` reduced to the five members the region calls); `@graph graph` is added before the `if`

the two adds on heads[i] (rdf:first, rdf:rest) are one `+{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 }`; the two single adds (rdf:nil for an empty list, the anchor) stay one `+{ }` each, as there is no second property on their subject
`ns_rdf["nil"|"first"|"rest"]` becomes `rdf:nil|first|rest` through `@prefix rdf:` (pyRdfa's ns_rdf is that namespace); `ns_rdf` is still imported by both sides but unused on the ldpy side
`vals == None` kept as is (a Python test on data, not an RDF operation); BNode() list heads kept in Python, since they are built before the triples and indexed (heads[i+1])
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the `if vals == None` / else branches merge. `vals = state.get_list_value(prop) or []` makes the empty-list case go through the general code: `heads` is then `[ns_rdf["nil"]]`, the inner loop writes nothing, and the anchor writes exactly the `(origin, prop, rdf:nil)` triple of the old None branch (the driver's EX.emptyList case). The comment of the empty-list case is kept above that line.

optimized.py, also: `for i in range(0, len(vals))` + `vals[i]` becomes `for i, val in enumerate(vals)`, and the rdf:first/rdf:rest pair becomes one `graph += [...]`. The BNode heads stay a list built in advance, because each node is read twice (heads[i] and heads[i+1]). rdflib's Collection was not used: on an empty list it anchors a dangling BNode instead of rdf:nil.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph graph`, one `+{ {heads[i]} rdf:first {val} ; rdf:rest {heads[i+1]} }` per element and one anchor island. A Turtle collection `( … )` cannot take a list of runtime length. No exception to the symmetry rule.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py is a copy of optimized.py: BNode, graph, state and ns_rdf are all used.
optimized_header.ldpy: ns_rdf leaves the shim import (replaced by `@prefix rdf:`, which is used).
